title: Truly Indian Launches Costco-Exclusive Dual Naan Pack For Midwest Diwali Shoppers
excerpt: The limited-time 24-oz eight-count pack pairs four Garlic and four Tandoori Plain naans at a stated $4.99 suggested price in Midwest Costco warehouses.
body:
• Truly Indian announced a Costco-exclusive Dual Naan Pack for Midwest warehouses, timed for Diwali: a 24-oz, eight-count pack with four Garlic and four Tandoori Plain naans.
  • The suggested retail price stated in the announcement is $4.99, and the pack is available for a limited time at Costco locations across the Midwest.
  • For Midwest diaspora shoppers: this is the pack to look for in the frozen aisle at your local Midwest Costco — the announcement does not list individual warehouses, so check your store while the limited run lasts.
  • The brand says the naans are made in India by artisans, hand-stretched and baked in a clay tandoor, then blast frozen; they are described as vegetarian and certified Kosher and Halal.

Truly Indian announced the launch of its Dual Naan Pack at Costco warehouses across the Midwest, just in time for Diwali, in a November 11 announcement distributed by EIN Presswire and carried by WCIA and Middletown Life.

Made exclusively for Costco, the 24-oz pack holds eight naans — four Garlic and four Tandoori Plain — at a suggested retail price of $4.99, the announcement said. It described the pack as one of the first variety naan packs in U.S. retail, intended so families can put two varieties on the table without buying two packages. The launch follows the debut of the brand's 24-count Samosas and 16-count Handmade Garlic Naan in other Costco divisions, according to the announcement.

What is in the pack

The Garlic Naan is the brand's number one seller, topped with garlic and cilantro, the announcement said. The Tandoori Plain Naan is described as a tandoor-baked crust brushed with butter. The wider Truly Indian naan portfolio listed in the announcement also includes 4-count Garlic and Tandoori Plain packs, Vegan Green Chili Naan, Vegan Tikka Masala Naan and Vegan Butter Chik'n Naan.

"When I watched our naans being made, I was deeply moved. What I saw wasn't machines but kind, hardworking artisans preserving tradition by hand."

— Rasa Kumar, Senior Vice President, Truly Indian

Kumar said the company's facilities employ mostly women and source from local farmers, and that the pack was created so more families can enjoy that quality during Midwest festive-season celebrations.

How the naans are made, as the brand describes it

According to the announcement, Truly Indian naans are made from scratch in India by generational artisans who hand-stretch each piece and bake it in a traditional clay tandoor oven, then blast freeze them. The announcement describes them as vegetarian, certified Kosher and Halal, glyphosate-free and low glycemic, made with locally sourced Indian ingredients, and suitable with curries and soups, grilled meats and vegetables, or as a base for pizzas, sandwiches and wraps. Those are the brand's own descriptions in its announcement.

Where and when to find it

The announcement says the Dual Pack is available for a limited time at Costco locations across the Midwest. It does not name individual warehouses or give an end date, and it does not state availability outside the Midwest. Midwest readers should check their local Costco's frozen section during the Diwali season rather than assuming every warehouse carries it.

Truly Indian is the U.S. retail brand of ADF Foods, a fourth-generation, family-owned food company founded in 1932, according to the announcement. ADF Foods says its portfolio of more than 400 frozen and shelf-stable products is available in more than 55 countries.
